exercises.instruction: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first.

items.prompt: The misunderstanding was my fault, so I apologised.
Jane won the tournament, so I congratulated her.
answers: I congratulated her on winning the tournament.

items.prompt: He has enemies, and he has a bodyguard to protect him.
answers: He has a bodyguard to protect him from his enemies.

items.prompt: Sandra eats only bread and eggs.
answers: Sandra lives on bread and eggs.

items.prompt: You can't say that the bad weather is my fault.
answers: You can't blame me for the (bad) weather.
You can't blame the (bad) weather on me.

items.prompt: The police thought my friend had stolen a car.
answers: The police suspected my friend of stealing a car.
The police suspected (that) my friend had stolen a car.
